label: token after p (original phase) or first copied token; highly sparse, unexplained selectivity
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.02% of steps). About 61% of activation mass is on original-phase steps right after an input p (strongest at t=3, and when the current token is v/q/y/b/c, especially in p p X contexts), and about 29% is at step L+1, when the first original token is fed back in. Here the first token is often v/l/x/h, and the sequence usually contains r or p early on. It never fires at t=0-1, on the delimiter, or past recall_idx 3, and it is rare in digit-heavy sequences. Even so, it fires on under 1% of the steps that match these contexts. The narrowest clean rule (p p followed by v/q/y/b/c) reaches 40% precision but only 15% mass recall, so what actually triggers it is not captured. Activations are tightly bunched (median 0.12, max 0.20), and I did not find a clear magnitude modulator.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: prev_tok=p (+4.60), prev2_tok=p (+3.83), phase=0 & in_tok=b (+3.46), orig0=v (+3.46), orig0=h (+3.38), recall_idx=-1 & in_tok=y (+3.36). Lower it: orig1=2 (-2.82), prev2_tok=v (-2.75), prev3_tok=v (-2.51), orig1=f (-2.17).
